summary: Introductory partner discovery between Redwood (AE + SE) and Sapphire Accelerator to explore GPU reseller / integration possibilities. Discussed partner motion (reseller vs OEM), technical integration points (VPC, private deploy, onboarding workflow), high-level benchmarks, security/compliance needs (SOC2, SSO/SAML, KMS), and commercial signals. Agreed to run an initial benchmark and exchange security docs and a draft reseller agreement.
topics: Technical integration: APIs, private deployment (VPC), on-prem packaging
Security & compliance: SOC2, KMS, SSO, audit logs
transcript:
[00:00] Maya (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Maya Patel from Redwood Inference here, AE on partner motions. We also have Daniel Cho our SE.
[00:12] Priya (Sapphire): Hi Maya, hi Daniel. Priya Rao—Head of Partnerships at Sapphire Accelerator. Luca and Jamal are with me.
[00:22] Luca: Hey all.
[00:25] Jamal: Morning.
[00:30] Maya: Quick agenda — intro + partner models, technical fit, security/compliance, next steps. Is that good?
[00:36] Priya: Yep thats perfect. We're primarily exploring two things: 1) a reseller/managed offering where we bundle GPUs + Redwood to our mid-market, and 2) a tighter OEM-ish integration for a handful of enterprise accounts.
[00:52] Daniel: Great, from a tech standpoint, good to know both motions, they map to different integration surfaces. Reseller is usually API + self-serve onboarding to your customers, OEM often needs private deployments or VPC-peered integrations.
[01:10] Jamal: On our side, the ask is we need an option where we can offer single-tenant stacks for regulated clients, maybe on their VPCs or our co-located racks. How flexible is Redwood Private?
[01:25] Daniel: Redwood Private supports customer-managed networking and on-prem packaging. We do have an air-gapped option for very regulated setups, and KMS/HSM integrations for keys. There are some ops tradeoffs — e.g., full on-prem requires infra coordination and a longer lead time.
[01:42] Luca: How does routing and fallback work? If we route through your hosted endpoints and there's a spike, can requests fail over to a smaller quantized variant?
[01:52] Maya: Yes we have smart routing — policy-based. You can set a preference for latency or cost, and we can fallback to compatible model variants. There is also prefix and KV cache to reduce token costs for repeated contexts.
[02:06] Priya: The security side is big for our clients — SOC2, ISO. We also need SAML SSO for our internal portal. Do you have SOC2 reports and an SSO connector?
[02:20] Daniel: We do have SOC2 Type II and can share an evidence pack. SAML / SSO and RBAC are supported in the console, plus audit logs and token-level retention controls. I can send the security packet after the call.
[02:35] Priya: Good. Also curious about pricing signals. If we resell, what kind of margin or partner discount do you offer?
[02:44] Maya: We have partner tiers — we can provide a reseller discount and co-sell credits. We should follow up with a commercial one-pager. Early pilots often run on dedicated slot commitments.
[02:55] Jamal: For the benchmark we'd like to see throughput for our generative recommendation workload — average seq len ~350 tokens, batch sizes up to 16, with KV cache usage. Typical inference mix is 60% chat, 40% single-turn.
[03:12] Daniel: That helps. Does your workload use off-the-shelf LLama-like models or custom finetunes?
[03:20] Luca: Mix — base open models with our finetuned heads. We can provide model artifacts or a compatible container.
[03:27] Daniel: Perfect — for benchmarking we'll want a sample model binary or an ONNX export, sample traces, and a dataset. We'll do run configurations across quantized variants and dedicated capacity.
[03:38] Priya: Timeline wise — ideal pilot start in July, production by Q4 if all goes well. Procurement window is typically 6–8 weeks.
[03:47] Maya: That seems reasonable. We should plan the tech deep dive week of June 23rd; Daniel can run the benchmark with Luca.
[03:55] Priya: Works for us.
[04:00] Maya: A couple of clarifying questions: 1) Do you want us to support billing to you as reseller or pass-through to end customers? 2) For private deployments, is colocation or VPC peering preferred?
[04:12] Priya: For reseller we want to bill through Sapphire — consolidated billing. For OEM pilots, probably VPC peering in customer accounts.
[04:23] Daniel: Noted. Also flagging a potential friction: if you want co-located racks on your side, kernel-level optimizations and driver versions need alignment. That can create a couple weeks more to the timeline.
[04:37] Jamal: Understood.
[04:40] Maya: On commercial — we'll send a starter reseller agreement (draft) and partner playbook that outlines lead flows, margins, and SLAs.
[04:50] Priya: Can you put in the playbook example SLAs? Our enterprise customers ask for 99.9 uptime and latency targets.
[04:58] Maya: Yes, we have SLA templates. For Dedicated we typically commit to 99.9 with burst capacity options and an escalation path.
[05:08] Luca: Are there any known limitations around sequence lengths or attention optimization for long sequences? We have a subset of use cases with 2k tokens.
[05:18] Daniel: Our runtime supports longer sequences but performance varies; we select kernels and quantization per workload. For 2k tokens we'll look at performance and possible offload patterns.
[05:28] Priya: On security, Jamal — do you have specific questions?
[05:32] Jamal: A few: KMS integration details, audit log granularity, and whether we can manage keys in our HSM. Also certification of the private package.
[05:41] Daniel: KMS integrations and HSM are supported for Private. Audit logs include token-level ops, model loads, and admin actions. I'll attach the schema in the packet. Certification for private packages is a joint effort — we'll provide the bundles and test checklist.
[05:56] Priya: Good. Any existing customers using a reseller model we can reference?
[06:00] Maya: We have a couple of mid-market partners in EMEA — I'll share anonymized case notes.
[06:07] Priya: On commercial math — for an 8x A100-equivalent dedicated pool what are ballpark unit costs?
[06:14] Maya: I'll run initial economics and share a ballpark number — depends on commit length and region. Roughly we can provide a per-hour committed cost and apply reseller tier discounts.
[06:26] Jamal: For benchmarks can you run both hosted API and dedicated pool to show delta in latency and cost?
[06:32] Daniel: Definitely — we'll provide run results for hosted vs dedicated with quantized variants.
[06:38] Priya: One operational question: how do software updates and model rollouts work in Private deployments?
[06:45] Daniel: We support rollout policies: canary, A/B, and immediate rollback. For Private, upgrades can be scheduled; for air-gapped there's a controlled package update process.
[06:58] Maya: Quick note, transcription may have small errors — apologies if some names get munged.
[07:02] Priya: No worries.
[07:05] Daniel: Moving to logistics — what access can you give us for the benchmark? A container registry, dataset S3, or a dummy workload?
[07:14] Luca: We can provide a private S3 bucket with restricted creds, and a docker image with the finetuned head. We'll coordinate with Jamal.
[07:23] Daniel: Excellent. We'll also need expected concurrency and failure modes.
[07:28] Jamal: Concurrent requests up to 100 for the recommender, but peak sustained is closer to 40–50. Failure modes: network retries and cold-starts are most important.
[07:38] Daniel: We'll simulate cold starts and KV cache warm/cold states in the benchmark.
[07:45] Priya: On legal — do you require an NDA before sharing customer traces?
[07:50] Maya: If it's PII or sensitive, yes. For model artifacts it's usually fine but we'll accept whatever you prefer.
[07:58] Priya: We'll mark dataset as sensitive and run under NDA.
[08:02] Maya: Perfect. I'll circulate an NDA template if you want.
[08:06] Priya: Please do.
[08:09] Maya: Recap of next steps: Maya to send partner one-pager + draft reseller agreement + NDA; Daniel to prepare benchmark plan; Luca/Jamal to share registry and sample traces; schedule tech deep dive wk of June 23.
[08:24] Priya: That matches our thoughts.
[08:27] Jamal: Quick technical Q — how do you handle KV cache across multi-tenant hosts? Is it per-tenant isolated?
[08:35] Daniel: Yes per-tenant isolation. For Dedicated it's customer-owned cache. For hosted we handle prefix-aware caching and strict isolation.
[08:43] Priya: Any red flags or concerns you foresee?
[08:47] Daniel: The main ops risk is co-located rack compatibility and certifying drivers. Also data governance for the OEM model.
[08:56] Maya: Commercially the lead time for Dedicated commitments can be a blocker for some customers — that's why the reseller option is attractive short-term.
[09:05] Priya: Understood.
[09:08] Maya: Any other questions from the Sapphire side?
[09:12] Priya: Not right now.
[09:14] Luca: None.
[09:16] Jamal: All good.
[09:18] Maya: Great, thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the packet and draft docs.
[09:22] Priya: Thanks, talk soon.
[09:25] [end of recording note: conversation continued with brief side-chat about calendar scheduling; transcript truncated to core meeting content]
